analysis.investment_thesis: Nazara trades at 133x earnings and 2.98x book — more than 5x the Graham Number of ~₹53 — with a 9-year net profit CAGR of negative 2.7%, offering no margin of safety whatsoever. This is pure speculation dressed as growth investing, and the disciplined value investor should not touch it at any price near current levels.
key_strengths: Low financial leverage (D/E 0.06) — balance sheet is not burdened by debt
Revenue CAGR of 25.5% over 9 years demonstrates real commercial scale in gaming
OCF positive all 5 recent years — the business does generate some real cash
key_risks: Earnings are illusory: net profit fell from ₹75 Cr (2024) to ₹51 Cr (2025) despite revenue growing; operating margin is a paltry 1.98%
Serial equity dilution — ₹946 Cr financing inflows in 2024, ₹805 Cr in 2025 — existing shareholders are constantly bearing dilution to fund acquisitions
Massive negative free cash flow in 2025 (-₹82 Cr) driven by ₹1,139 Cr of investing outflows, suggesting growth is entirely acquisition-driven, not organic
red_flags: P/E of 133.6 — nearly 9x my maximum threshold of 15; P/B of 2.98 — double my ceiling of 1.5
Graham Number ≈ ₹53 (sqrt(22.5 × EPS ₹1.37 × BVPS ₹91.5)); stock trades at ₹273 — a 5x premium to intrinsic asset value
Net profit 9-year CAGR is negative (-2.7%) — the company earns less today in real terms than it did in 2016
'Other Income' of ₹80 Cr in 2025 (treasury/investment returns) exceeds operating income expansion — operating business barely profitable
No dividend history — management retains all capital yet delivers ROE of only 2.90%, destroying shareholder wealth
analysis.detailed_analysis:
Mr. Market has been extraordinarily generous to Nazara shareholders, assigning a ₹10,126 Cr market cap to a business earning ₹51 Cr in net profit — a P/E of 133.6. My Graham Number, calculated from EPS of approximately ₹1.37 and book value per share of approximately ₹91.5, yields roughly ₹53. The stock would need to fall 80% merely to reach fair value by my standards. The ROE of 2.90% is a damning indictment: this management has received hundreds of crores in equity capital from shareholders across multiple fundraises and has compounded it at a rate below a fixed deposit. That is not a business; it is a charitable transfer of wealth from public shareholders to founders and investment bankers.

The acquisition binge is particularly alarming — investing cash outflows of ₹612 Cr in 2024 and ₹1,139 Cr in 2025 are funded entirely by new equity issuances, not retained earnings. A company that cannot grow without continuously diluting its owners is not compounding wealth — it is redistributing it. The net profit actually declined from ₹75 Cr to ₹51 Cr in 2025, and a meaningful portion of reported profits comes from "Other Income" (₹80 Cr in 2025), which likely represents returns on the cash raised from equity offerings, not from the gaming business itself. No dividends, negative long-run earnings growth, excessive valuation, and serial dilution — this stock fails every quantitative screen I apply.
